note: Advanced singing made musical: a fast run and an octave tune to open the range, then guide tones and improvising over a ii-V-I that the app plays as accompaniment, with the line sung from a staff. The run's range is stated, every target is named with the chord it lands on, and each block says what to sing on.

exercise.title: Guide tones over ii-V-I, then your own line
exercise.focus: Pentatonic run · octave tune · guide tones over Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 · your own line in F
exercise.why: Singing the 3rds and 7ths through a ii-V-I trains you to hear the chord changes.

sections.text: Press Play below to hear the run, then start the mic and sing it lightly on "ah" at the tempo shown. It goes from La below Do up to the high Do, and each pass starts a semitone higher: five passes, the last one reaching the top of your range.
Press Play below to hear a tune that leaps to the octave, then start the mic and sing it on "oo", which keeps the top note light. Watch where your top note lands on the staff.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the chords. Sing one long note per chord on "ah": {{4}} (F) over Dm7, still {{4}} over G7, then {{3}} (E) over Cmaj7. Then sing the other line: {{1}} (C) over Dm7, {{7}} (B) over G7, and {{7}} again over Cmaj7.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the same changes in F: Gm7, C7, Fmaj7. The notes change, the pattern doesn't. Make up your own line on any vowel, starting each chord on one of its lit notes: {{4}} or {{1}} over Gm7, {{7}} or {{4}} over C7, {{3}} or {{7}} over Fmaj7. Leave space between phrases.
